images.caption: New land from NISAR backscatter. Top: radar brightness (HH, median of 5 ascending passes before and 4 after the eruption); sea is dark, rock bright. Right: new land in orange (26.5 ha, seen on both ascending and descending passes), the pre-eruption coast in blue. Bottom: the Sentinel-2 composites on the same 3.8 km crop, with the same outlines.
images.source: NISAR L2 GCOV (provisional), NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, via ASF DAAC: 18 passes, tracks 10A, 119D; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel-2 data (ESA), via Element 84 Earth Search

note: NISAR backscatter (GCOV, both look directions, 5 before, 4 after on 10A; 5 before, 4 after on 119D) shows 26.5 ha of new land on the coast of Anak Krakatau, 24.8 ha of it on the W, SW and S shore: sea-dark on every pass up to 2026-09-02, rock-bright from the first pass after the eruption (2026-09-06) on. Badan Geologi measured 32.8 ha (NW-W-SW) from Sentinel; we catch 81% of that (16.6 ha with the strictest test). Sentinel-2 agrees: those cells were water-coloured before and rock-coloured after. The two new islets reported 760 m NW and 495 m SE of the coast don't show: no new bright spot at sea within 500 m of either pin on any pass, though a rock a few tens of metres across 770 m off the SE shore shows on most passes, before and after. The islets may be too small or too low to stand out from the sea, or lie elsewhere (only their distances from the coast were published).
